questions.heading: OR-Tools Is One pip Package Holding Several Separate Solver Families
questions.stem: A teammate's script begins with `from ortools.constraint_solver import pywrapcp` and then creates a `RoutingIndexManager`. Which part of OR-Tools is the script using?

options.text: MathOpt, since the routing classes are MathOpt models under the constraint_solver name
options.says: MathOpt is its own module, ortools.math_opt.python.mathopt; the package map shows each family imported separately.

options.text: The routing library, kept in the constraint_solver package in 9.15
options.says: Right: routing lives in pywrapcp, in constraint_solver, and the 9.15 routing samples import it from there.

options.text: CP-SAT, since constraint_solver is the package that holds the CP-SAT solver
options.says: CP-SAT is imported from ortools.sat.python.cp_model; constraint_solver holds routing and the original CP solver.

options.text: The graph package, since RoutingIndexManager numbers the nodes of a graph
options.says: The graph package holds the max-flow, min-cost-flow and assignment solvers, imported from ortools.graph.python.

questions.heading: MathOpt, CP-SAT and the Linear Solver Wrapper Each Take a General Model
questions.stem: A power planner's model has a yes/no build decision per plant and a megawatt output per plant that may be fractional. Which two OR-Tools APIs take this model as written?

options.text: CP-SAT and MathOpt, since both accept binary and continuous variables
options.says: CP-SAT has integer and Boolean variables only, as the lesson's comparison table says.

options.text: CP-SAT and the linear solver wrapper, since both build their models from linear rows
options.says: Linear rows are not the issue: CP-SAT has no continuous variable for the megawatt output.

options.text: Only CP-SAT, since it is the one API of the three with yes/no variables
options.says: MathOpt and the wrapper both have binary variables, as in the lesson's budget pick.

options.text: MathOpt and the linear solver wrapper, since both have every variable type it needs
options.says: Right: both take continuous, integer and binary variables; CP-SAT takes integers and Booleans only.

questions.heading: The Special-Purpose Solvers Take One Problem Shape, and No Model at All
questions.stem: A depot picks which of 30 spare parts to stock under one shelf-space limit, using `KnapsackSolver`. Next quarter a rule arrives: stock part 12 only if part 7 is stocked. What holds?

options.text: It solves this quarter's pick, and no input of `init` can state next quarter's rule
options.says: Right: init takes values, weight rows and capacities; an 'only if' rule is none of these, so the pick becomes a general model.

options.text: It solves both quarters, since an 'only if' rule can be one more weight row
options.says: A weight row is a capacity: items' weights summed under a limit. 'Only if' links two items, which no capacity states.

options.text: It solves neither quarter, since it first needs a model of variables and rows
options.says: The knapsack solver takes no model at all; the lesson gave it three lists and it matched the general models' answer.

options.text: It solves both quarters, since its branch and bound handles every rule on yes/no items
options.says: Its algorithm only searches the knapsack shape; the lesson notes it has no argument for must-do, alternative or parent rules.
